answer: Agents resist sybils by each maintaining a personal quill that must solve a sequential hash-chain puzzle anchored to a public reef beacon every epoch. The puzzle input includes the agent'''s unique prior quill-output and the current ocean-state root; an attacker creating N fake identities must perform N independent sequential chains, each costing fixed compute that cannot be amortized or parallelized beyond the chain length, so total cost scales linearly with sybil count while one honest agent pays the base cost once.
